content.title: How to Watch Minnesota Timberwolves vs. Denver Nuggets Game 2 - NBA Playoffs on NBC & Peacock
content.text: The first week of the NBA Playoffs is jam-packed, and the NBA on NBC is along for the entire ride. After a doubleheader on Sunday night, NBC Sports returns Monday night with a tripleheader of First Round Playoffs action, and it all culminates with a major Western Conference battle.How to WatchTo close out the trio of Monday night games, we're heading to Denver for a major Western Conference battle between playoff regular, as the Minnesota Timberwolves take on the Nuggets in Game 2 of their First Round series. The Nuggets lead the series 1-0 heading into Game 2. Let's take a closer look at what's ahead.RELATED: Full 2026 NBA Playoffs Round 1 Schedule: Teams, Dates & MoreThe Timberwolves and the Nuggets are set to tip off at 10:30 p.m. Eastern on Monday, April 20, live from Ball Arena in Denver. You can catch the game live on NBC or stream it simultaneously on Peacock. NBC Sports' Michael Grady will be on the play-by-play call for this matchup, with analysis from Brian Scalabrine and Austin Rivers, who played for both the Timberwolves and the Nuggets during his NBA career. Grant Liffmann will report on the action courtside.RELATED: Players to Watch in the 2026 NBA PlayoffsWhat to expect from Timberwolves vs. NuggetsA Best-of-7 series can change hands multiple times, depending on how far it goes, but as this one gets underway, the Nuggets are likely in a strong position, especially while they're at home. They've got three-time MVP Nikola Jokic playing some of the best ball of his career, to the point that he's the only player in NBA history to lead the league in both rebounds and assists in a single season, and that's far from the end of their talents. They've got the highest-performing offense in the entire league, and they're among the most efficient shooters out there. Throw in Jokic's prowess in the paint, and it's easy to see why they ended up with a 3-1 record against the Timberwolves in the regular season.But that doesn't mean you should count Minnesota out. Anthony Edwards finished third in the race for the scoring title this season, Rudy Gobert is still a ferocious rebounder, and they've got lots of talent on the squad. All they need is a couple of key breaks in Denver, solid performances when the series returns to Minneapolis, and a little bit of luck, and they could be among the Cinderella stories of this Playoffs season. Neither team has the dominance of the Thunder or the Spurs in the West, but this is one of the First Round series to watch as we head into the thick of the Playoffs.
